title: Junos Interfaces: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: One physical port can carry many separate networks. Junos splits every interface into two parts. Let's decode the name.

scenes.heading: The letterbox with slots
scenes.narration: Picture one letterbox at the door with several slots inside, one for each department. The box is the hardware, and each slot is its own compartment. The letterbox itself is the physical interface. Each slot is a logical unit. The address goes on the slot, never the box.

scenes.heading: Special interfaces
scenes.narration: Two special interfaces are worth knowing. The loopback is always up, so it's ideal for router I Ds. And an aggregated interface bundles several ports into one, using L A C P. The loopback needs no cable. Aggregated links add bandwidth and backup. Only the ae interface gets the address.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three common traps. A logical unit always belongs to a physical port. The address goes on a unit, never the bare port. And only the aggregate gets an address, not its members.

items.right: Always tied to a physical port

items.wrong: Put the IP on the physical port
items.right: Put it on a logical unit

items.wrong: Every ae member needs the same IP

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva Junos interfaces lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Names follow type, then F P C, P I C and port, then the unit. The address goes on the logical unit. Loopback is always up, and ae bundles links. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva Junos interfaces lab.
